_comment: MP-423 — edge functions that are ACTIVE in prod with NO source in this repo.
These are NOT tolerated defects that got baselined for convenience. Each one
is source code that exists in exactly one place on earth: the Supabase edge
runtime. If prod loses it, it is gone. And because every repo guard walks
supabase/functions, NONE of them has ever graded these files —
check-ilike-user-input (the MP-422 wildcard that minted a session on a
the enum/CHECK vocabulary guards, check-relation-exists. All blind, all six.
The baseline is a NAMED SET, not a count (MP-356/MP-357: a count-only floor
is fungible — a real regression can sit red until an unrelated pay-down
absorbs it, and a brand-new ungoverned endpoint passes green so long as the
total does not rise). A slug not listed here fails the next deploy.
This file shrinks by RECOVERING source, never by adding slugs.

MP-476 (2026-09-08): daily-brief PAID DOWN — supabase/functions/daily-brief/ now exists, so the guard sees repo source for it. Removed here per the rule above: this file shrinks by recovering source. Separately, ACTIVE count fell 259 -> 232 and the novel orphan mp457-service-branch-probe was DELETED from prod rather than baselined — it was MP-457's own throwaway probe, whose source said 'inert; delete when a working Supabase PAT exists'. Backup of its body: ~/business-ops/website-integrity-bot/retired-function-backups/.

MP-478 (2026-09-08): SOURCE RECOVERED for all 5, via scripts/recover-edge-function-source.py using the scoped Management credential MP-476 put on the machine. The mirrors are at supabase/_recovered-orphans/<slug>/index.ts and every slug STAYS LISTED HERE -- recovery is not payment. What the runtime returns is the TRANSPILED module (comments and logic intact, TypeScript types erased, formatting normalised), measured against check-stale-onboarding whose real source is in the repo. A mirror is paid down only when a human restores the types and moves it to supabase/functions/<slug>/. The mirrors are deliberately OUTSIDE supabase/functions/ because deploy-supabase.yml deploys every directory under it on BOTH the deploy-all and deploy-changed paths -- committing them there would push a machine-recovered transpilation over live prod the moment a working Management PAT exists. MP-479 closed the consequence: the guards were pointed AT the mirrors instead of the mirrors being moved into the deploy path.

MP-479 (2026-09-08): the five guards now READ these mirrors — check-ilike-user-input, check-phone-gateway-source, check-empty-catch, check-enum-filter-literals (enum + CHECK halves) and check-relation-exists all scan supabase/_recovered-orphans/, with roots derived from THIS FILE so the scanned set and the manifest cannot drift. All five orphans come back CLEAN on those classes, mutation-proven non-vacuous (an injected dead relation and an invalid enum literal both go red naming the mirror path). REFUSED the handoff's design of moving the mirrors into supabase/functions/ behind a deploy skip-list: all three deploy paths are structurally confined to supabase/functions/ (deploy-all cd's into it, deploy-changed's awk requires $1==supabase && $2==functions, only_function resolves under it), so a mirror outside it is un-deployable BY CONSTRUCTION -- a skip-list would trade that for a maintained set plus a drift guard, which MP-356/MP-357 showed is fungible. check:orphan-mirror-containment now enforces that placement as a contract rather than an accident, and verifies each recovered body against its sha so a mirror cannot be edited to silence a guard: a finding in a mirror is a fact about PRODUCTION and the remedy is a deploy, never a repo edit. Added banner_bytes/body_sentinel/body_split because the sha256 describes the bytes BELOW the banner and that rule existed only in prose -- the obvious whole-file checker disagrees with the manifest on all five and reads as total drift on an intact set, which is exactly what MP-479's first measurement did.
